title: auth: unify header semantics for org/project scopes, scoped tokens, CORS and request-signing/nonce headers
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: As part of continuing work to make Redwood's API surface both OpenAI-compatible and production-safe, customers asked for clearer, consistent header semantics for org/project-scoped requests, token scoping, CORS behavior, and a lightweight request-signing/nonce mechanism to prevent replay and make proxying safer. This PR unifies header handling across the main proxy, openai-compat layer, and SDKs, and documents the expected semantics for downstream integrations. Motivation: Previously there were subtle differences in how project keys vs org keys were accepted (x-redwood-project, x-redwood-org, Authorization bearer), inconsistent handling of CORS preflight for cross-origin initialized keys, and no standardized nonce/signature header for optional request signing. Those differences led to developer confusion and a couple of customer bugs when routing via gateways. Summary of changes: - Add canonical header parsing layer (pkg/auth/headers.go) used by redwood/proxy and redwood-openai-compat to normalize incoming headers: Authorization, X-Redwood-Project, X-Redwood-Org, X-Redwood-Token-Scope. - Introduce scoped token semantics: implement X-Redwood-Token-Scope parsing and enforcement in the token introspection path (scopes are still token-level metadata; enforcement only applied where route requires project OR org scope). - Standardize CORS behavior: preflight now returns Allow-Origin derived from origin->project mapping when present; credentials policy clarified for project-scoped requests; updated tests to guard cross-origin usage. - Add optional lightweight request signing headers: X-Redwood-Nonce and X-Redwood-Signature (HMAC-SHA256 over path+nonce+timestamp using shared signing key). Signing is opt-in and documented for customers using reverse proxies/Gateway with client-side signing. - OpenAI compatibility layer updates: ensure the compatibility proxy accepts both standard Authorization Bearer and X-Redwood-Project headers equivalently, while still enforcing scope semantics. - SDK updates: python + ts SDKs add helpers to set project headers, construct signature headers, and opt-in cors-friendly request mode. - Docs: redwood-docs/api/auth.md added with migration guide, recommended header patterns, and security notes. - Tests: unit and integration tests added for header normalization, scoped token enforcement, CORS preflight behavior, and signature verification. Migration notes and compatibility: - Backwards compatible: legacy Authorization bearer tokens continue to work. - Project-scoped header (X-Redwood-Project) is treated as an alternative to embedding project in the token; when both are present they must match. - Nonce/signature headers are opt-in; if a route requires signature and it is missing, the request is rejected. - CORS semantics tightened: customers using cross-origin keys should verify the origin->project mapping configuration in console; default origin allowlist remains restrictive. Testing and rollout: - CI: added unit + integration suites; initial flaky test in cors suite fixed by adding deterministic origin fixtures. - Canary rollout planned: enable header enforcement behind a feature flag for 24h in staging, then progressively enable in Canary region for non-critical endpoints before global rollout. - Rollback: feature-flag controlled; revert to previous header normalization if we see false positives.

review_comments: Ari Kaplan (reviewer): Can we confirm the security impact when both Authorization and X-Redwood-Project are supplied and mismatch? Recommendation: reject if mismatch.
Maya Chen (author): Implemented strict mismatch reject (see headers.go line 84) and added unit test ensuring mismatch returns 401.
Diego Morales (reviewer): CORS preflight tests flaky in CI, failing on parallel runs. Suggest deterministic origin fixtures.
Maya Chen (author): Fixed test by serializing the fixture setup and added a retry harness for the integration test. CI green locally.
Lena Park (security): What's the threat model for X-Redwood-Signature key material? Make sure keys are treated as secrets and not logged.
Maya Chen (author): Signature key is read from KMS-backed secret; middleware explicitly redacts signature headers from logs. Added docs note in auth.md.
Ari Kaplan: Approve after docs and SDK helpers included.
release_notes: Unified header semantics for org/project keys and optional request-signing support. Adds X-Redwood-Token-Scope, X-Redwood-Nonce, and X-Redwood-Signature headers; standardizes CORS preflight behavior and documents migration steps.
